mappings.note: Which wish Bismil feared would go unfulfilled - the pupil must find it in the quoted letter among four plausible options. LO-87 close reading; rejected LO-86, the whole text's gist.
The mother's greatest injunction is stated in the text. LO-87.
Who taught the sisters - a stated detail. LO-87.
From whom the mother learned housework - a specific point in the passage. LO-87.
Where the grandmother summoned her sister - a stated detail. LO-87.
Which song Bismil wrote ('Sarfaroshi ki tamanna') is stated in the lesson material. LO-87.
Whom a quoted sentence refers to - locating the referent in the text, LO-87.
Why he asked his mother to bear it with patience requires reading his whole argument and concluding; the key is 'all of the above', so LO-87 rather than LO-86.
Year of birth, from the lekhak-parichay - a stated point. LO-87.
His age at execution is stated in the author note. LO-87.

Names the lesson's vidha. LO-89 is the outcome about reading compositions of various kinds. NB the key is WRONG: it gives yatravrittant, whereas 'Meri Maan' is an atmakatha - and this chapter's own long answers call it Bismil's atmakatha.
Which Congress session he wished to attend - a stated detail. LO-87.
Who disapproved of his activities is stated in the text. LO-87.

Match-the-following glossing four references (Devanagari, Arya Samaj, Mazzini, Gobind Singh) - unfamiliar words and their meanings, LO-90. Rejected LO-87: the work is lexical. NB the printed key is garbled - it reprints the whole table instead of giving the pairings.
Gadyansh on the mother teaching herself to read, three sub-questions - sustained close reading for specific points, LO-87.
Gadyansh with five MCQ sub-questions: most are comprehension (LO-87), but two ask the meanings of 'urin' and 'avarnaniya' (LO-90). Both cited so neither half is left unmapped.
Gadyansh on his last letter, three sub-questions - close reading for specific points, LO-87.
Two-part item on how the mother adapted to the household and educated herself - both answered from the text, LO-87.
'apne vichar prakat kijiye' asks for the pupil's own reflection in writing - LO-97. Rejected LO-87, since the answer is not a point in the text.
Which of his qualities impressed YOU and why - the pupil's own written comment, LO-97.
How the mother made him courageous is drawn from the text's account - locating points and concluding, LO-87.
'bataiye kaise' asks for textual evidence that she valued education - LO-87.
'hum kaise kah sakte hain' asks for evidence of her liberal outlook - close reading and conclusion, LO-87.

Asks the pupil to hunt the lesson for paired/compound words (dant-phatkar, kaam-kaaj, uthna-baithna) and list them: LO-90 for the word curiosity, LO-100 for the point the stem itself makes about economical word use in writing. Rejected LO-95, which covers muhavare and lokokti, not compounding.
Why he refused to sign the vakalatnama is narrated in the lesson. LO-87.
Bhagat Singh's remark is quoted in the lesson material - locating it, LO-87.
The title of his autobiography and its effect are stated. LO-87; rejected LO-89, since the question asks for the title, not the genre.
Whose grace he credited for his courage is stated in the text. LO-87.
'is path se kya prerana milti hai' asks for the whole lesson's message - LO-86, forming a sense of the composition's point, rather than LO-87's specific detail.
